MC	<p>d4d7_0538</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7439b6;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jy, ++, jy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6131_a85d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #97401c;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #97401c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #97401c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d39e_fb16</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8c3192;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pr, ++, pr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8b95_d471</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #66600a;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #66600a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #66600a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8341_02e9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7439b6;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f4a5_a6a5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #19687a;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #19687a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #19687a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #992f68;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #992f68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ace4_9c68</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7439b6;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4059_ff53</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8c3192;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hx, ++, hx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5397_c3bb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>12eb_4afc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #325da0;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #325da0;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #325da0;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mt, ++, mt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ab1a_41f7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2a6d3c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #992f68;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #992f68;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #992f68;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, py, ++, py"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #66600a;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #66600a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #66600a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8c3192;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>fb8a_b1cc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #97401c;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #97401c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #97401c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1205_c973</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8c3192;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jr, ++, jr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8307_69d5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #325da0;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #325da0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>fd9d_74d3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #66600a;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #66600a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #66600a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8c3192;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pr, ++, pr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #325da0;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #325da0;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7d62_b923</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2a6d3c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cm, ++, cm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>685f_5b93</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #97401c;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #97401c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #97401c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6397_171c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2a6d3c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #66600a;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #66600a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #66600a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #992f68;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #992f68;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #992f68;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bj, ++, bj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">4,200</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>5949_eb28</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. MC	<p>68fb_00f9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #325da0;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #325da0;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b51c_a059</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, wy, ++, wy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes W and Y</h5>	distance = <table style="border-collapse: collapse; display: inline-table; vertical-align: middle;"> <tr><td style="border-bottom: 1px solid black; text-align: center;">&half;(4,126) + MC	<p>85c4_6131</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mn, ++, mn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>02c1_f6bb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4b6915;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4b6915;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6915;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7439b6;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>41db_aefb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pw, ++, pw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes P and W</h5>	distance = <table style="border-collapse: collapse; display: inline-table; vertical-align: middle;"> <tr><td style="border-bottom: 1px solid black; text-align: center;">&half;(1,206) + MC	<p>d2d9_410a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #19687a;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #19687a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #19687a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jm, ++, jm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9927_ca69</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hm, ++, hm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e571_a9f5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bx, ++, bx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a661_fef1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4b6915;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4b6915;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6915;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d4cbf;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d4cbf;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cm, ++, cm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>61df_fe57</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #325da0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #325da0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #325da0;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, py, ++, py"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a62a_78b3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>4f09_eb0a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #325da0;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #325da0;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #325da0;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jm, ++, jm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7439b6;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7439b6;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ct, ++, ct"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7039_d2df</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hx, ++, hx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #66600a;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #66600a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #66600a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4b6915;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4b6915;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>884e_4489</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a12f3c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12f3c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22648b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kr, ++, kr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #66600a;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #66600a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2a6d3c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3192;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8c3192;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>47ca_3070</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2a6d3c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2a6d3c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #992f68;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #992f68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #992f68;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dk, ++, dk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
